title: 1990 AMC 8 Problem 12
statement: There are twenty-four \(4\)-digit whole numbers that use each of the four digits \(2,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) and \(7\) exactly once. Listed in numerical order from smallest to largest, the number in the \(17\)th position in the list is

solutions.text:
Each leading digit accounts for \(6\) of the \(24\) numbers. Positions \(1\)–\(6\) begin with \(2\), positions \(7\)–\(12\) begin with \(4\), and positions \(13\)–\(18\) begin with \(5\).

So the \(17\)th number is the \(5\)th one beginning with \(5\): \(5247,\) \(5274,\) \(5427,\) \(5472,\) \(5724\). The fifth is \(5724\).

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: The \(24\) numbers split into four blocks of \(6\) by their leading digit
Positions \(1\)–\(6\) start with \(2\), \(7\)–\(12\) start with \(4\), \(13\)–\(18\) start with \(5\); find the \(5\)th number starting with \(5\)
